drafted_from: tool row in tools/office-files/tool-rows.json, do-work/describe-presentation-runtime-surface.mjs and test/apply-presentation-edits.test.mjs (run on its stand-in runtime)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me the property names my presentation runtime /work/runtime.mjs exposes for a slide, a shape's text and speaker notes, using /work/in.pptx." It reads the tool's row and runs describe-presentation-runtime-surface.mjs on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads or rewrites one file on the person's own computer and prints what it found or changed.
instructions: 1. Have a presentation runtime module (any module that exports FileBlob and PresentationFile with importPptx and exportPptx) and a small deck.
2. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:describe-a-presentation-runtime} and runs its `run` command with the module path and the deck path.

3. Read the JSON it prints: the property names on the first slide, its first text shape, that shape's text object, the speaker notes and the notes text frame, plus the first shape's text and the notes text. Nothing is changed.
4. Use those real names when you write an edit request for tool:edit-a-presentations-text.

worked_examples.title: List the names a stand-in runtime exposes
worked_examples.ask: Show me the property names my presentation runtime exposes for a slide, a shape's text and speaker notes.
worked_examples.given: From tools/office-files/test/apply-presentation-edits.test.mjs, whose stand-in runtime keeps a deck as a JSON file; I ran the probe on that runtime with a three-slide deck whose first slide has the texts "Welcome to the harbour tour" and "Doors open at nine" and the notes "Greet the group". Command: node tools/office-files/do-work/describe-presentation-runtime-surface.mjs /work/runtime.mjs /work/in.pptx.
